knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6.5,

This vignette follows the workflow of the ICAR project *Development of
AI-driven solutions for quantifying runoff induced soil loss and nutrient
loss*: quantify runoff, soil loss and nutrient loss with their uncertainty,
decide where conservation is needed, and choose where new measurements would
help most.

```{r setup}
library(terravai)
```

## 1. A micro-watershed

`dm_simulate_watershed()` builds an 81 ha micro-watershed (30 m cells) with
terrain, vegetation, soils and rainfall, "true" runoff, soil loss and N, P, K
losses, and 40 runoff plots with measurements.

```{r}
ws <- dm_simulate_watershed(n_side = 30, seed = 3)
ws
g <- ws$grid
xy <- g[, c("x", "y")]
```

## 2. Runoff by the curve number method

Annual runoff is approximated by 25 storms. The curve number is uncertain, so
it is given as a distribution; the result is a predictive distribution of
runoff.

```{r}
cn <- dm_uncertain(g$cn, sd = 4, lower = 30, upper = 100, coords = xy)
runoff <- dm_runoff_cn(P = g$rain / 25, CN = cn, n_draws = 300, seed = 1)
runoff$draws <- 25 * runoff$draws
runoff$mean <- 25 * runoff$mean; runoff$sd <- 25 * runoff$sd
summary(runoff$mean)
```

## 3. Soil loss by RUSLE, with uncertainty

The LS factor comes from the terrain, the C factor from NDVI and the K factor
from soil texture and organic carbon. Erosivity and cover are uncertain.

```{r}
soil <- dm_rusle(R = dm_uncertain(g$R, cv = 0.15, lower = 0, coords = xy),
                 K = g$K, LS = g$ls,
                 C = dm_uncertain(g$C, sd = 0.05, lower = 0, upper = 1, coords = xy),
                 n_draws = 300, seed = 2)
soil
```

## 4. Where is soil loss above the tolerable limit?

```{r, fig.height = 4.2}
dec <- dm_decide(soil, dm_loss_tolerance(T_limit = 11.2, ratio = 3))
summary(dec)
plot(dec, "act")
plot(dec, "p_wrong")
dm_narrate(dec, area = "the micro-watershed")
```

## 5. Nutrient loss

**Formula-based mass balance:** sediment-bound loss from soil loss, nutrient
content and enrichment ratio, plus dissolved loss in runoff.

```{r}
N_formula <- dm_nutrient_sediment(soil, content = 0.08, unit = "percent",
                                  enrichment = 1.6, seed = 3)
summary(N_formula$mean)
```

**Empirical ICAR-IISWC equations** relating N, P and K loss to soil loss or
runoff percentage:

```{r}
N_emp <- dm_nutrient_empirical(soil, "N", "soil", seed = 3)
summary(N_emp$mean)
head(attr(dm_nutrient_coef(), "jumps"))
```

The empirical segments are not continuous at their breakpoints (see the
`jumps` table and the Caution section of `?dm_nutrient_empirical`), so
estimates close to 5, 10 or 20 t/ha need care.

Decision on nitrogen loss:

```{r, fig.height = 4.2}
plot(dm_decide(N_formula, dm_loss_nutrient(15, "N")), "p_need")
```

## 6. Load at the watershed outlet

```{r}
cell_ha <- (ws$cell_size^2) / 1e4
dm_outlet_load(soil$mean, ws$to, delivery = 0.9, cell_area = cell_ha)
```

## 7. Where should new runoff plots go?

Value of information for the tolerance decision, from the Monte Carlo
ensemble of soil loss:

```{r, fig.height = 4.2}
v <- dm_voi(soil, dm_loss_tolerance(), method = "ensemble",
            candidates = seq(1, nrow(g), by = 3), seed = 4)
plot(v, main = "Value of a new runoff plot")
```

## 8. Is the model good enough? Formula versus measurements

Compare RUSLE with the "true" soil loss by accuracy and by decision regret:

```{r}
ev <- dm_evaluate(g$soil_loss,
                  list(rusle_decision = soil, rusle_plugin = soil$mean),
                  dm_loss_tolerance(), ratios = c(1, 3, 10))
summary(ev)
```

AI models trained on runoff-plot data (`dm_fit_qrf()`, `dm_conformal()`) can be
compared in the same way, and their predictions used in every step above.

## 9. Your own region

The same chain runs on real rasters anywhere, from a district in India to a
whole country, on projected or longitude/latitude grids:

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)}
dem <- terra::rast(nrows = 40, ncols = 40, xmin = 78, xmax = 78.04,
                   ymin = 30, ymax = 30.04, crs = "EPSG:4326")
terra::values(dem) <- as.numeric(outer(1:40, 1:40, function(i, j) 700 + 5 * i + 2 * j))
out <- dm_erosion_raster(dem, R = 900, ndvi = terra::init(dem, 0.35), K = 0.03,
                         P = dm_p_factor("contouring", 6))
terra::global(out[["A"]], c("mean", "max"), na.rm = TRUE)
```

Curve numbers and hydrologic soil groups for any land use and soil:

```{r}
hsg <- dm_hsg_texture(sand = c(70, 35, 20), silt = c(20, 40, 35), clay = c(10, 25, 45))
dm_cn_lookup(c("row_crops_contoured_good", "pasture_fair", "woods_fair"), hsg)
```
